tour.title: What Frigorino Is
tour.description: Start with the architecture docs, not the stub root README. The knowledge/ index catalogs every pattern, capability, and feature note, while Vertical_Slices.md is the authoritative contract for how the whole API is built: one file = one endpoint, with domain rules living in aggregate methods and factories that return FluentResults. Read these two first and the rest of the tour will click into place.

tour.title: Backend Composition Root
tour.description: Program.cs is the single ASP.NET Core host that assembles the entire backend. It registers every Infrastructure concern through Add* DI extensions (EF, auth, AI, file storage, telemetry), fixes the middleware order (session before authentication), wires each vertical slice into MapGroup route groups, and finally falls back to serving the React SPA. This file is the map of everything the tour explores next.
tour.languageLesson: ASP.NET Core minimal hosting composes the app as builder.Services (DI registration) then app.Use*/app.Map* (pipeline). Middleware runs in registration order, which is why UseSession must precede UseAuthentication.

tour.title: The Domain Core
tour.description: The innermost Clean Architecture ring holds framework-free business rules. The Household aggregate root exposes a factory plus membership methods that enforce role permissions and the last-owner invariant, returning FluentResults instead of throwing. DomainErrors defines the marker error types (AccessDeniedError, EntityNotFoundError) that slices later pattern-match onto HTTP status codes — the seam between domain logic and the web layer.
tour.languageLesson: FluentResults models success/failure as a returned Result<T> object rather than exceptions, so domain rules stay pure and callers branch on typed errors instead of catching.

tour.title: A Vertical Slice, End to End
tour.description: Now see the pattern in the flesh. CreateHousehold is the canonical write-via-factory slice — its rules-as-comments header is the authoritative slice template for the codebase. AddMember is the most complex variant, resolving a target user across aggregates and branching three ways on the aggregate method's result. ResultExtensions is the shared glue that converts a failed domain Result into the right ValidationProblem/404/403 response.

tour.title: Persistence with EF Core
tour.description: Building on the aggregates from Step 3, the ApplicationDbContext aggregates every entity DbSet, applies the per-entity IEntityTypeConfiguration mappings, and centrally auto-stamps CreatedAt/UpdatedAt inside SaveChangesAsync so handlers never touch timestamps. Its DI extension parses the Postgres connection string (accepting a postgres:// URL) and is one of the Add* calls you saw in Program.cs; migrations run automatically at startup.

tour.title: Authentication and User Sync
tour.description: Frigorino authenticates via Firebase JWTs. FirebaseAuth configures JWT bearer validation and hooks OnTokenValidated to lazily upsert the local Users row once per real login, gated on the token's auth_time claim so it fires per-login, not per-request. DevAuthHandler is the opt-in bypass used by agents and fresh clones, swapping the real Firebase flow for a fixed dev-user without changing any slice code.

tour.title: Multi-Tenant Household Context
tour.description: Every request runs inside a household tenant. CurrentUserService reads the caller's identity straight from JWT claims and deliberately injects no DbContext. CurrentHouseholdService keeps the active household id in the HTTP session (with a durable fallback on the User row) and exposes the role/access checks that household-scoped slices depend on — which is exactly why session middleware had to be ordered before auth back in Program.cs.

tour.title: Pluggable Infrastructure Capabilities
tour.description: The Infrastructure layer bolts optional capabilities onto slices through keyed, flag-gated Add* extensions. Item classification and file storage each register a real vendor implementation only when their key and Enabled flag are set, otherwise a no-op Null/Log implementation — keeping the domain vendor-agnostic. The cron-triggered ExpiryNotificationScan shows the background-work rule in action: it claim-slots a NotificationDispatch ledger row and sends synchronously in-request rather than via a lossy in-memory queue.

tour.title: The SPA Boots Up
tour.description: Cross into the frontend. main.tsx is the SPA entry point: it fires a wake-ping at the sleeping backend, initializes observability, auth, i18n, push, and PWA, then mounts the TanStack Router app inside its providers. The __root route renders the shared Navigation layout, applies the persisted language, and hides the nav on auth/onboarding paths — the shell every feature route slots into.
tour.languageLesson: TanStack Router is file-based: files under src/routes/ compile into a typed route tree (routeTree.gen.ts). __root.tsx is the always-mounted layout wrapper that all other routes nest beneath.

tour.title: The Generated API Client
tour.description: This is where the frontend closes the loop back to Step 4's endpoints. From the backend's OpenAPI spec, hey-api generates a typed SDK (one function per endpoint), matching DTO types, and TanStack Query bindings (query-key factories, query options, mutation functions) — all committed and refreshed with a single `npm run api`. No hand-written fetch code and no drift between client and server contract.
tour.languageLesson: Code generation from an OpenAPI schema makes the server the single source of truth: the wire contract is enforced at compile time in TypeScript, so a renamed or removed endpoint surfaces as a type error rather than a runtime 404.

tour.title: Feature Data Hooks and Route Guards
tour.description: Feature modules consume the generated bindings through thin TanStack Query hooks. authGuard is the router beforeLoad guard that waits for the auth store to settle before resolving or redirecting. useCurrentHousehold reads the server-resolved active tenant (Step 7), and useHouseholdLists builds on it to fetch that household's shopping lists — the same household context, now viewed from the client side.

tour.title: How It's Tested
tour.description: The Testing doc draws the line the whole suite follows: xUnit + FakeItEasy for pure aggregate and slice unit tests, and Reqnroll + Playwright + Postgres Testcontainers for anything that touches real database behavior (no SQLite or EF-InMemory). ArchitectureTests is the guardrail that mechanically enforces the Clean Architecture dependency direction you've been tracing — Domain depends on no framework, and neither Infrastructure nor Features references Web.

tour.title: How It Ships
tour.description: Finally, packaging and delivery. The multi-stage Dockerfile publishes the .NET backend and builds the Vite SPA in parallel stages, then copies the SPA build into wwwroot of a minimal non-root .NET 10 runtime image serving on port 8080 — one deployable that contains both halves of the tour. docker-compose spins up Postgres for local development, and the CI workflow runs frontend checks, .NET unit/ArchUnit tests, and the Playwright integration suite in parallel on every PR.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds use several FROM stages: heavy build tooling (SDK, Node) lives in builder stages, and only the compiled artifacts are copied into a slim final runtime image — cutting image size and attack surface.
